claims.text: TOR-TILD's EAM references do not capture the full diversity of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid.
A deep neural network potential trained on diverse ab initio liquid configurations can serve as the reference state in thermodynamic integration calculations for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Training on diverse liquid configurations enables the neural network potential to represent a broader spectrum of local atomic environments.
The broader representation of liquid atomic environments improves phase-space overlap with the ab initio target system.
Improved phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to an EAM reference.
Using the neural network reference will improve liquid-state free-energy accuracy.
A potential trained broadly on liquid configurations will also improve solid-state free-energy accuracy.
The method is applicable to compositionally complex refractory high-entropy alloys near melting temperatures exceeding 3000 K.
Liquid-phase atomic diversity is particularly high in compositionally complex refractory high-entropy alloys near their melting points.
The intervention's benefits will be greatest for multicomponent systems with substantial atomic configurational complexity.
The intervention's benefits may be less pronounced in binary or single-component systems.
The intervention's benefits may be less pronounced at substantially lower temperatures.
The neural network reference may reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 20–40%.
Thermodynamic-integration path mismatch can be quantified using cumulative free-energy differences.
Direct ab initio calculations or experimental melting-temperature measurements can benchmark the resulting free-energy predictions.
